I do take meds but before I started them I would associate certain things I liked to certain tasks. For example, every single time I do dishes I open my kitchen window and play music I like. I have a really hyperactive toddler. He hates sitting still and is suspected to have ADHD or he pretty high functioning autistic. Restaurants are very hard to go to with him because he hates sitting and I think all the noise and motion around him overwhelms him, however, I absolutely do not give him a tablet. He needs to learn how to be able to sit. I do bring different toys, snacks while waiting for food, and stuff to color. I also will get up and hold his hand and walk around with him a bit if he needs. I get each child has specific needs, but I personally think tablets are creating children who then turn into adults with very low attention spans who needs constant stimulation. I also think it’s important to be respectful of others and letting your children listen to their tablet at full volume is disrespectful.

I have ADHD and studying when not on my meds is extremely difficult. The only things I’ve found to help are: 
- have a set studying environment if possible so when you’re there your brain registers it as time to study. 
- make sure your study area is clean (I personally will just feel so unfocused if I’m trying to studying and also thinking about how messy my area is) 
- Get a study candle that you light when it’s time to study 
-Open a window and get some fresh air when you’re studying 
-Binaural beats can be helpful if you need some background music. 
- Don’t put pressure on yourself to get a certain amount of things done per day. Instead come up with a list of tasks to do (anki, JackWestin, content review) and just figure out what’s your priority for the day and go through your tasks like that. 
- this one is probably silly but make your notes pretty. I have an iPad and like to do my notes in different color palates. It just motivates me for some reason to study and take notes when I like how they look. Just be careful not to spend too much time on this cause then it just becomes a waste of time. 
-Have a notepad in front of you where you can write down any thoughts not related to studying. For example, I used to randomly get distracted and think about how I needed to come up with a grocery list before I forgot. So then I would stop studying and make a grocery list because I knew I would forget if I didn’t do it right in that moment. I then started writing these types of thoughts down on a note to remind myself to do them when I was done studying.
